🤖 OA is already mostly personal: `npx @openagt/start` in the Vike folder pushes nothing on its own.

- The agents' records (tickets, queue, logs) stay on your machine unless you turn sharing on.
- The default skills are linked into each run, hidden from git.
- Your phone and server read your laptop's runs live, with nothing shared.

One gap: a skill you tick in the dashboard is committed into the repo, and reaches agents only once you push it.

Idea, one rule: everything stays on your machine until you share it.
- A ticked skill is "Just me" by default (linked into runs like the default ones). "Add to the project" commits it for everyone.
- One Sharing page per project lists all of it: records to this computer / origin, and each skill Just me / Everyone.
- Later: records to a private repo of your own (e.g. `brillout/vike-openagent`), so the history stays while your laptop is off.

Thoughts?

Topics: install, skills
Issue: [#2239](https://github.com/openagt/openagent/issues/2239)

# Personal installation instead of a per-project one

## TLDR

Let one person use OpenAgent on a project without adding it to the project's repository. The requester wants to use some of OA's skills on Vike (for example, account rotation) without pushing OA onto the project's other contributors.

OA is already mostly personal: `npx @openagt/start` pushes nothing on its own. The records (tickets, queue, logs) stay on the machine unless sharing is turned on, the default skills are linked into each run and hidden from git, and other devices read the laptop's runs live. The one gap: a skill ticked in the dashboard is committed into the repository, and reaches agents only once pushed.

Proposed rule (in the issue, awaiting the requester's thoughts): everything stays on your machine until you share it.

- A ticked skill is "Just me" by default, linked into runs like the default ones; "Add to the project" commits it for everyone.
- One Sharing page per project lists it all: records on this computer or on origin, and each skill Just me or Everyone.
- Later: records kept in a private repository of one's own (e.g. `brillout/vike-openagent`), so the history stays while the laptop is off.

## Why it matters

People who don't own a project, or who don't want to impose OA on everyone else working on it, can't use OA there. A personal installation lets one contributor adopt OA on a shared project without the others having to agree.
EOF
cat > /tmp/t2242.md <<'EOF'
Topics: accounts, skills
Issue: [#2242](https://github.com/openagt/openagent/issues/2242)

# Account rotation as a skill: `@openagt/skill-accounts`

## TLDR

Account rotation is built into the runner (`agent-driver/core/src/accounts.ts`) and only works for runs OA starts. Move it into a skill package built like `skill-scheduler`:

- An `accounts` command: `add`, `list`, `remove`, `use-first`, plus `next` and `limited` for the runner.
- A SKILL.md, so an agent can add or list accounts when the person asks ("add my second Claude account").
- The Accounts settings move into the package's own dashboard part.
- The runner calls the package instead of having rotation built in.
- `accounts run claude`: the person's own terminal `claude` on the next free account; when it hits its limit, it continues on the next one with `--resume`. No OA install needed.

To check first: can a wrapper catch the limit in Claude Code's interactive screen? (Easy in `-p` / stream-json.)

## Why it matters

Asked for in #2239: people want account rotation on a project without installing OA there. As a standalone skill it works for anyone's own `claude`, and the runner gets simpler.
